newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain gives final approval to new pension law.
newsitem.headline: Spain gives final approval to new pension law.

text.p: Spain's parliament gave its final approval on Thursday to a new Pension Law, aiming to reduce public expenditure while guaranteeing the starting age to claim a pension would be mantained.
The process which began with a pensions agreement known as Toledo Pact in 1995, also ended with the innovative introduction of an automatic revaluation clause linked to inflation.
Following are the main points summarising the new Pension law, according to an Economy Minister statement:

-- "Financial separation", which will be gradual and must be implemented by the year 2000. According to this universal benefits, such as health expenditures and non-contributory pensions will be financed by taxes while contributory benefits will be paid directly with wages contributions.

-- Constitution of reserves, through a reserve fund charged to social contribution surpluses resulting from Social Security Budget accounting in each economic period. The Government will approve the materialisation of these reserves.
-- Contributions. A sole contribution ceiling will be created for all professional categories.
-- Period of calculation. The number of minimum years required for entitlement to a pension, which will gradually be increased from the current eight years to 15 years.
-- Legal retirement age will remain at 65. The government could opt for subsidies, tax-breaks or deductions when a worker decides to remain in work up to that age, pending consultation with unions.
-- Proportion of entitlement. After 35 years of payment of social contribution, 100 pct. After 25 years, 80 pct and after 15 years, 50 pct.

-- Stricter control for pensions for the handicapped. A "sickness list" will be drawn up by the government following a proposal by the Social Security to define disability and its different degrees. Pensions for the handicapped will automatically become Old Age Pensions when the beneficiary turns 65, without loss of any prior rights.
-- Pensions for the widowed. Minimum pensions when the beneficiary is under 60 years of age will be brought in line over a four year period with those received between the ages of 60 and 64.
-- Allowances for orphans. To be extended to the age of 21 and to the age of 23 if both parents are deceased, as long as the beneficiary is not in work.

-- Automatic increases. For the first time ever increases will be legislated on a permanent basis. Contributory pensions will increase at the beginning of each year, according to CPI forecasts. If the accumulated CPI -November to November- overshoots forecasts, an adjustment will take place. If it is lower, the difference will be absorbed when calculating the benefit growth for the following year.
